title: Local Offline Continuity
summary: Core and Observer preserve worktree isolation, bounded history and local retrieval without network services.

localContinuity.process: The local service owns observation and retrieval independently of network availability.
localContinuity.core: Use the same deterministic Core, profile policy, generated snapshots, strict freshness, Brief, Pack, Impact and local task-continuity contracts.
localContinuity.localAuthority: A current result describes its local root and profile. It grants no publication authority over another worktree.
localContinuity.publicationPolicy: Only the granted local publisher may refresh a managed index. Reads do not acquire hidden write authority.
localContinuity.storage: Keep snapshots, bounded observation state and history outside consumer source. They are not a source backup or unlimited journal.

identity.worktree: Keep independent root, profile, Observer identity and lifecycle bindings. Equal folder names do not establish identity.
identity.gitOptional: Ordinary directories without Git remain supported; source fingerprints and workspace identity are sufficient.

outbox.persistence: Preserve existing unacknowledged entries and destination pins; an unavailable legacy peer does not authorize history deletion.
outbox.bounds: Retain byte, entry and generation limits; report exhaustion or gaps explicitly. Local retrieval has an independent storage budget.
outbox.compatibility: The historical loopback metadata transport remains explicit and opt-in. No receiver, source synchronization or remote account service is supplied.

authority.localProof: Observe only explicitly granted roots. Retrieved evidence never grants execution or publication rights.
authority.facets: Report source freshness, retrieval readiness, history and storage separately.

acceptanceCases: Local retrieval and sampling work offline.
Separate worktrees retain distinct identities and history.
Failures preserve pending observations and identity pins.
No implicit source export, account login or cross-host synchronization.
